scope: Original source-only exFAT format CPU; no runtime, hardware, native or full-system qualification

source_navigation.draft_status: NONMATCHING; algorithm and source input addresses inspected directly in authenticated image4 A32 instructions

publication_boundary: No firmware table bytes are published. ExfatTables borrows the caller's owner-supplied image. The caller authenticates SHA-256 before from_image4; the constructor independently checks exact image length and table rolling fingerprints, which are not cryptographic authentication. The unsafe mapped constructor requires authenticated immutable readable X-M1 spans for its returned lifetime.

public_interface.entry: format_exfat(io: &mut impl filesystem_runtime::SectorIo, volume: &mut filesystem_format::VolumeDescriptor, layout: filesystem_format::Layout, control: &filesystem_format::FormatControl, tables: ExfatTables<'_>) -> Result<(), filesystem_format::FormatError>
public_interface.mounted_scan: scan_free(io: &mut impl SectorIo, volume: &mut VolumeDescriptor, control: &FormatControl) -> Result<(), FormatError>; read-only root-directory traversal to the active bitmap entry, FAT-chain traversal of noncontiguous bitmap clusters, trailing invalid bitmap bits excluded, capacity publication only on complete successful scan. Requires mounted Layout root, FAT and cluster geometry.
public_interface.provider: SectorIo read/write use filesystem_format::Sector and consecutive full-sector byte slices; sector_bytes must be 512; flush must report actual provider completion.
public_interface.integration: Filesystem runtime selects Layout and passes mandatory ExfatTables only for ExFat. SD/FTL routing remains in the canonical SectorIo implementation.
public_interface.publication: Volume layout, next-free cluster, free count, metadata status and write state are published only after all writes, canonical flush and actual allocation-bitmap readback scan succeed. Partial medium writes survive errors; no rollback or fabricated success.

derived_behavior: Zero inclusive range 0 through partition + 2*fat_pages + 3*cluster_pages - 1 before MBR and BPB writes.

Write boot sectors at partition and partition+12; eight signed extended boot sectors per copy; OEM sector at offsets 9 and 21; zero reserved sectors 10 and 22; repeated rotate-right/add checksum words at offsets 11 and 23.
Boot checksum excludes byte offsets 106, 107 and 112. The all-zero reserved sector does not change the checksum after 512 rotations.
Initialize FAT entries 0..4 to fffffff8, ffffffff, ffffffff, ffffffff, ffffffff.
Bitmap zeroing rounds the truncated clusters/8 byte count into sectors; root directory reports rounded-up bitmap byte length.
Stream exactly 0x16cc source upcase bytes with zero padding; checksum covers only the unpadded source bytes.
Root first byte is 3, not a substituted 0x83 volume-label entry; bitmap and upcase entries begin at offsets 32 and 64.
Root data location follows bitmap and upcase allocation; initial bitmap marks all system clusters allocated.
Retained Layout descriptor addresses preserve actual u16 partition truncation, including 65536 becoming zero in descriptor-derived FAT/data addresses; on-disk BPB partition remains full-width.
intentional_replacement_rules: Reject non-exFAT layouts, non-512-byte providers and unsupported cluster geometry before writes.
Propagate provider write, flush and readback failures as Write, Flush and Scan; cancellation is checked before each I/O step.
Use actual bitmap readback for free-space publication instead of proprietary mapping-workspace and cluster-scan CPU calls.

Mounted bitmap scanning uses a constant-space cycle-detecting FAT cursor; invalid clusters, short chains, cycles, missing active bitmap and undersized bitmap data fail without capacity publication. Root and bitmap placement are read from mounted metadata, not formatter constants.
